tools.name: open_ainecto_panel
tools.description: Opens the AiNecto panel beside the conversation: the signed-in user's notifications, comments they can reply to, and their kanban work, kept up to date while it is shown. Hosts that cannot show panels get the same summary as get_my_work_summary (only that project's items once a project is chosen). panel names the project (needsProject with candidates when several fit) and artifactVersion, the newest Claude app panel page; with artifactPage: true it also returns that page (html, capabilities) for publishing the panel as a claude.ai artifact. Read-only: nothing is marked read; the user marks items read or replies in the panel itself.

projectUuid.description: The project whose panel to open (from list_projects). Give it when the user names a project or the project you are working in is clear. Without it: the only project you can open, or a list of candidates.

artifactPage.description: true adds panel.artifactPage: html (the Claude app panel page for this project, large) and capabilities, for publishing the panel as a claude.ai artifact. Give it only when publishing or republishing the panel.

tools.name: create_comments
tools.description:
Add comments, questions, or replies to a document or a kanban card (cardUuid). Anyone who can read it may comment and reply. Set parentCommentId to reply to a top-level comment. To mention people, get their userId and displayName from list_mention_candidates, write @<displayName> in the body, and list their userIds in mentionUserIds (clientMutationId is then required). Items are applied in order and each one commits on its own; results report each item (ok, or status and error).

Retries: send a unique clientMutationId with each write; if you retry the same call (for example after a timeout or lost response), send the same clientMutationId and the server returns the first result instead of running it again.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

items.description: Comments to add, applied in order

body.description: Comment text (plain text, 1..10000 characters). To mention someone, include @<displayName> exactly as returned by mcp__ainecto__list_mention_candidates.

kind.description: COMMENT (default) or QUESTION. A reply (parentCommentId) is always COMMENT. A QUESTION can later be resolved with mcp__ainecto__resolve_comments.

parentCommentId.description: Reply to this top-level comment id (from mcp__ainecto__list_comments). Replies are one level deep: replying to a reply is rejected. The thread's original author and earlier repliers get a notification email (except people mentioned in this reply, who get the mention email instead).

mentionUserIds.description: userIds to mention (from mcp__ainecto__list_mention_candidates). Each one's @<displayName> must appear in body; newly mentioned people get a notification email.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Required when mentionUserIds is not empty; reuse the same value when retrying the same item so the mention email is not sent twice.

mailLanguage.description: Language of the comment notification email (mention or reply). Defaults to en.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key for this call (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Reusing it with the same arguments returns the first result (marked idempotentReplay); reusing it with different arguments is rejected with 409.

tools.name: delete_comments
tools.description:
Delete your own comments on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid). Only the author can delete. A resolved question and a top-level comment that still has replies cannot be deleted. Each id is applied on its own; results report each id.

Retries: send a unique clientMutationId with each write; if you retry the same call (for example after a timeout or lost response), send the same clientMutationId and the server returns the first result instead of running it again.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key for this call (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Reusing it with the same arguments returns the first result (marked idempotentReplay); reusing it with different arguments is rejected with 409.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: List the active comments on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid), oldest first, including replies (a reply has parentCommentId set; replies are one level deep). Each comment has id, kind (COMMENT or QUESTION), body, author, mentions (userId, label and position in the body), and for questions questionState (UNANSWERED, ANSWERED, RESOLVED) and resolvedAt. Anyone who can read it can list its comments.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

tools.name: list_mention_candidates
tools.description: List the people you can mention in comments on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid): userId, displayName and jobTitle (null = not set) — jobTitle helps tell people with the same name apart. Only people who can read it are listed — for a card, the people who can read its board, which are also the people a card can be assigned to. To mention someone, write @<displayName> exactly in the comment body and pass their userId in mentionUserIds of create_comments or update_comments. Page with nextCursor while hasMore is true.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

query.description: Name filter, 0..100 characters. Omit or leave empty for the first page of everyone.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous page (same parent and query).

tools.name: list_my_comments
tools.description: List the comments, questions and replies the signed-in user wrote, across documents and kanban cards in one list, newest first by default — call it when the user asks things like "what did I comment on?", "which of my questions are still open?" or "find the comment I left about ...". Each item has commentId, kind (COMMENT or QUESTION), body, parentCommentId (set on a reply), resolved (for a top-level question: true once resolved; null otherwise), createdAt, updatedAt and target {type (DOCUMENT or KANBAN_CARD), documentUuid (for a card, its board), cardUuid (cards only), title, url}. Only comments on what you can read now are listed; deleted comments are not. Filters combine with AND. Read the next page by passing nextCursor as cursor (hasMore says whether there is one). To read a whole thread use list_comments with the target's documentUuid or cardUuid.

order.description: Sort by when the comment was written: newest (default) or oldest first.

projectUuid.description: Only comments in this project. With workspaceUuid too, both must match. A workspace or project you cannot see matches nothing.

kind.description: Only this kind: COMMENT or QUESTION.

resolved.description: Only your top-level questions that are resolved (true) or still open (false). Comments and replies are left out when this is given.

since.description: Only comments written at or after this ISO-8601 time, e.g. 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z.

until.description: Only comments written before this ISO-8601 time.

target.description: Only comments on documents (DOCUMENT) or on kanban cards (KANBAN_CARD).

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous response, to read the next page. Keep the other arguments the same.

tools.name: resolve_comments
tools.description:
Mark questions on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid) as resolved. Only top-level comments with kind QUESTION can be resolved, and it needs edit access to the document or board (readers can comment but cannot resolve). Resolving cannot be undone. Each id is applied on its own; results report each id.

Retries: send a unique clientMutationId with each write; if you retry the same call (for example after a timeout or lost response), send the same clientMutationId and the server returns the first result instead of running it again.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

ids.description: Question ids to resolve (top-level comments with kind QUESTION)

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key for this call (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Reusing it with the same arguments returns the first result (marked idempotentReplay); reusing it with different arguments is rejected with 409.

tools.name: update_comments
tools.description:
Edit your own comments on a document or a kanban card (cardUuid). Only the author can edit, and only while they can still read it. A resolved question and a top-level comment that already has replies are locked. Items are applied in order and each one commits on its own; results report each item.

Retries: send a unique clientMutationId with each write; if you retry the same call (for example after a timeout or lost response), send the same clientMutationId and the server returns the first result instead of running it again.

documentUuid.description: Document UUID the comments belong to. Give this or cardUuid, not both.

cardUuid.description: Kanban card UUID the comments belong to (from kanban_list_cards). Anyone who can read the card's board may comment. Give this or documentUuid, not both.

body.description: New comment text (replaces the old text).

mentionUserIds.description: The complete set of userIds mentioned after the edit; omit to remove all mentions. Each one's @<displayName> must appear in body. Only people who were not mentioned before get a notification email.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Required when mentionUserIds is not empty; reuse the same value when retrying the same item so the mention email is not sent twice.

mailLanguage.description: Language of the comment notification email (mention or reply). Defaults to en.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key for this call (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Reusing it with the same arguments returns the first result (marked idempotentReplay); reusing it with different arguments is rejected with 409.

tools.name: conversation_get_messages
tools.description: Read messages of one conversation, always returned oldest first. Without afterSeq/beforeSeq: the most recent limit messages. Every conversation belongs to one AiNecto project: the project room (everyone who can open the whole project) and direct chats between two project members (only those two can read them). Each message has seq (increasing within the conversation), uuid, author {userId, displayName — null if the account was deleted}, body, at, registeredBy (how it was sent) and readCount (how many current members other than the author have read it; in a direct chat 1 means read). hasMore says whether more messages exist beyond this page in the direction you read. This does not mark anything read — call conversation_mark_read when the user has seen them.

afterSeq.description: Only messages after this seq, oldest first — to fill a gap after the last message you saw.

beforeSeq.description: Only messages before this seq — to page back through older messages.

tools.name: conversation_list
tools.description: List my conversations in one project: the project room first, then my direct chats (most recent first). Every conversation belongs to one AiNecto project: the project room (everyone who can open the whole project) and direct chats between two project members (only those two can read them). Each conversation has conversationUuid, type (PROJECT_ROOM or DIRECT), name (project name, or the other person's name), withUserId (direct chats), unreadCount, latestSeq, myLastReadSeq and lastMessage {seq, author, preview, at}. members lists the people who can open the whole project (userId, displayName, jobTitle to tell same names apart) — the people you can start a direct chat with. Messages are not marked read.

withUserId.description: Only the direct chat with this project member (userId from members). Empty list if there is none yet — conversation_send with to.userId starts it.

tools.name: conversation_mark_read
tools.description:
Move the signed-in user's read position in one conversation up to throughSeq (default: the latest message). The position only moves forward and never past the latest message; inbox notifications for this conversation up to that position are marked read too. Call it when the user has seen the messages, not merely because you fetched them. Anyone who can read the conversation (viewers too) may mark it read. Returns lastReadSeq, unreadCount and notificationsRead.

Retries: send a unique clientMutationId with each write; if you retry the same call (for example after a timeout or lost response), send the same clientMutationId and the server returns the first result instead of running it again.

throughSeq.description: Mark read up to and including this seq (the last message the user has seen). Default: the latest message.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key for this call (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Reusing it with the same arguments returns the first result (marked idempotentReplay); reusing it with different arguments is rejected with 409.

tools.name: conversation_send
tools.description:
Send one message as the signed-in user, to a conversation (conversationUuid) or to a place (to). Every conversation belongs to one AiNecto project: the project room (everyone who can open the whole project) and direct chats between two project members (only those two can read them). Sending needs edit rights on the project (viewers can read but not send); a direct chat's other person must still be a project member. The other person of a direct chat gets an inbox notification (messages within 5 minutes are one item); the project room sends no notifications yet. Returns conversationUuid, type, seq, messageUuid and at; your read position moves to your own message.

Retries: send a unique clientMutationId with each write; if you retry the same call (for example after a timeout or lost response), send the same clientMutationId and the server returns the first result instead of running it again.

conversationUuid.description: Send into this conversation (from conversation_list). Give this or to, not both.

userId.description: Direct chat with this project member (userId from conversation_list members) — found or started in the same call.

to.description: Where to send when you do not have a conversationUuid: {projectUuid, userId} for a direct chat, or {projectUuid, room: "project"} for the project room. Give exactly one of userId and room.

clientMutationId.description: Idempotency key for this call (visible ASCII, at most 128 characters). Reusing it with the same arguments returns the first result (marked idempotentReplay); reusing it with different arguments is rejected with 409.

groupUuid.description: Group UUID; null or empty string clears membership

height.description: Explicit height; omit to keep it derived from member nodes

tools.name: diagram_get_edge
tools.description: Read one diagram edge by its edge UUID (same fields as diagram_list_edges). Read only; needs read access to the diagram. Fails with 404 for an unknown edge.

tools.name: diagram_get_group
tools.description: Read one diagram group by its group UUID (same fields as diagram_list_groups). Read only; needs read access to the diagram. Fails with 404 for an unknown group.

tools.name: diagram_get_node
tools.description: Read one diagram node by its node UUID (same fields as diagram_list_nodes). Read only; needs read access to the diagram. Fails with 404 for an unknown node.

tools.name: diagram_get_pending_llm_requests
tools.description: List your own AI requests that are waiting (PENDING) or in progress (PROCESSING), for every service, not only diagrams: uuid, serviceCode, type, status, model and context. Read only — it does not claim anything; a request becomes PROCESSING only when a worker claims it through AiNecto's AI request API. Returns requests and count.

tools.name: diagram_list_edges
tools.description: List every edge (connector) of one diagram document: uuid, diagramUuid, fromUuid, toUuid, label, bridgeType, style, strokeColor, lineStyle, strokeWidth, arrowStyle, version. Read only; needs read access to the diagram. Fails when diagramUuid is not a diagram document. Returns edges and count.

tools.name: diagram_list_groups
tools.description: List every group of one diagram document: uuid, diagramUuid, name, color, width, height, parentGroupUuid, collapsed, depth, sortOrder, linkedDiagramUuid, linkMode, version and nodeUuids (the member nodes; each node also points to its group with groupUuid). Read only; needs read access to the diagram. Fails when diagramUuid is not a diagram document. Returns groups and count.

tools.name: diagram_list_nodes
tools.description: List every node of one diagram document: uuid, diagramUuid, type, text, shape, x, y, width, height, groupUuid, fillColor, strokeColor, textColor, version. diagram_apply_changes changes them. Read only; needs read access to the diagram. Fails when diagramUuid is not a diagram document. Returns nodes and count.

tools.name: diagram_submit_llm_result
tools.description:
Complete one of your AI requests that is PROCESSING by storing its result text and token counts; it becomes COMPLETED. The token counts are recorded only; no AI credits are charged (creditsCharged is ignored). It only stores the result and does not change any diagram by itself. Fails for a request that is not yours, is not PROCESSING, or whose context names a diagram you cannot edit. Returns uuid, status and the recorded token counts.

Retries: send a unique clientMutationId with each write; if you retry the same call (for example after a timeout or lost response), send the same clientMutationId and the server returns the first result instead of running it again.

cachedInputTokens.description: Cached subset of provider total input tokens

creditsCharged.description: Deprecated; ignored. No credits are charged.

tools.name: erd_apply_changes
tools.description:
Required single-call mutation path for ERD create/update/delete changes. Put tables, columns, indexes, refs, enums, enum_values, and table groups in one operations array and call this once.
Rules: (1) all data field names are snake_case; (2) for create, generate your own UUIDs and put them in data.uuid, then later operations in the same batch may reference those UUIDs without read-back calls; (3) enum values are separate enum_value operations, not inline on enum; (4) ref.relationship uses short dbdiagram-style symbols: >, <, or -; (5) ref_column operations map FK columns explicitly, never automatically.
Do not look for type-specific ERD CUD tools; this tool is the only ERD CUD entry point. If operations is very large, use request_upload_token with purpose=mcp.call and send the tools/call payload with curl to save LLM tokens.
One-call worked example:
{
  "documentUuid": "erd-doc-uuid",
  "description": "create users/posts ERD",
  "operations": [
    {"op":"create","type":"table","data":{"uuid":"tbl_users","name":"users","display_order":1}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_users_id","table_uuid":"tbl_users","name":"id","type":"bigint","is_pk":true,"is_not_null":true,"display_order":1}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_users_email","table_uuid":"tbl_users","name":"email","type":"varchar(255)","is_unique":true,"is_not_null":true,"display_order":2}},
    {"op":"create","type":"table","data":{"uuid":"tbl_posts","name":"posts","display_order":2}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_posts_id","table_uuid":"tbl_posts","name":"id","type":"bigint","is_pk":true,"is_not_null":true,"display_order":1}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_posts_author_id","table_uuid":"tbl_posts","name":"author_id","type":"bigint","is_not_null":true,"display_order":2}},
    {"op":"create","type":"column","data":{"uuid":"col_posts_status","table_uuid":"tbl_posts","name":"status","type":"post_status","is_not_null":true,"display_order":3}},
    {"op":"create","type":"enum","data":{"uuid":"enum_post_status","name":"post_status"}},
    {"op":"create","type":"enum_value","data":{"uuid":"enum_post_status_draft","enum_uuid":"enum_post_status","value":"draft","display_order":1}},
    {"op":"create","type":"enum_value","data":{"uuid":"enum_post_status_published","enum_uuid":"enum_post_status","value":"published","display_order":2}},
    {"op":"create","type":"ref","data":{"uuid":"ref_posts_author","name":"fk_posts_author","from_table_uuid":"tbl_posts","to_table_uuid":"tbl_users","relationship":">","on_delete":"cascade"}},
    {"op":"create","type":"ref_column","data":{"uuid":"refcol_posts_author","ref_uuid":"ref_posts_author","from_column_uuid":"col_posts_author_id","to_column_uuid":"col_users_id","display_order":1}}
  ]
}

Returns favorited: [{documentUuid, favorited: true, favoritedAt}] and count.

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description: Read new notifications for the signed-in user, oldest first and without gaps. The server remembers, per connection and per filter (kinds, workspaceUuids, projectUuids, directOnly, agent), how far you have acknowledged; a new filter starts from now. Each response carries ackToken: pass it as ack in your next call (with the same filter) after you have handled the batch — if you do not, the next call returns the same batch again (identify duplicates by id and seq; an item that comes back with a higher seq and a larger groupCount is an update of the same entry). Each item has id, seq, kind, at, summary (one line), actor, target (title and url only when you can read it now), action (what the user is asked to do) and humanRead. A DOCUMENT_UPDATED item (a document the user subscribed to was changed by someone else; changes within 10 minutes are one item) also has documentChange {changeCount, versionSummary — the name/description of a named version saved in that group, else null}. An item you can no longer read comes back as {id, seq, at, redacted: true}. This tool never marks anything read for the person (use mark_notifications_read when the user asks); open to-dos are in list_agent_todos. The same call repeated within 30 seconds returns the previous result without reading again, unless the inbox changed in between (a new or updated notification, a read, an ack); a call that carries ack is always read fresh. tools.name: kanban_apply_changes
tools.description:
Create, duplicate, edit, reorder and link cards on one kanban board in a single atomic call (at most 100 operations; if one fails nothing is applied and the error carries operationIndex and code). Creating, duplicating and editing cards needs edit access to the board; move with toBoardUuid moves a card to another board of the same project. The assignee may also check acceptance criteria and add result links (DELIVERABLE, REVIEW_RESULT, TEST_EVIDENCE). A TEST_EVIDENCE link records a test result you observed yourself and must carry a verdict (PASS or FAIL); the card's verificationState (kanban_list_cards detail) is computed from these links. create also sets assignee, requester, reviewers and watchers in the same call. To change a card's column, reassign it, accept, approve, block, watch and similar, use kanban_card_action. Results list each operation's card uuid, revision, status and sortKey.

Retries: send a unique clientMutationId with each write; if you retry the same call (for example after a timeout or lost response), send the same clientMutationId and the server returns the first result instead of running it again.

tools.name: kanban_card_action

tools.name: kanban_list_cards

Lists (boardUuid or none) return one short line per card: uuid, key (KAN-15 — the short id people use in chat; find a card by it with cardKeys, then use its uuid in the write tools), title, cardType, status, priority, assignee (name), assigneeAgent (name of the assignee's agent, if any), assignmentState (PENDING = not yet accepted), blocked and revision — open cards with cardUuids for the rest.
